description: Follow-up correctness defect from migrate-test-docker-stacks-to-mocker (deferral #337). Reproduced with Mocker 0.7.2: an alpine:3.20 Compose service whose healthcheck always exits 1 made 'mocker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 5' return success in 0 seconds, and inspect exposed no Health state. This is a false-success readiness contract, not merely missing test coverage. Group the unhealthy-fixture, capability detection/emulation, bounded timeout, and cleanup work here. Evidence: /tmp/mocker-negative-wait-probe.log (2026-08-16).

item_meta.blocked_reason: Measured locally on mocker 0.7.2: an alpine:3.20 service with healthcheck 'exit 1' made 'mocker compose up -d --wait --wait-timeout 5' return 0 in 0s; inspect exposed no Health state. A passing regression requires either an upstream Mocker healthcheck implementation/version or an explicitly scoped BenchBox healthcheck-emulation design. Real Docker is unavailable on this host. Evidence: /tmp/mocker-negative-wait-probe.log.

work_units.summary: Add a project-scoped fixture whose healthcheck deterministically never passes and records elapsed time plus exit status
Prevent Mocker --wait from reporting readiness when health cannot be observed, via a supported upstream version or an explicit BenchBox capability check/emulation
Assert bounded nonzero failure for the unhealthy fixture and retain a positive healthy-service control
Guarantee project-scoped teardown on success, timeout, and interruption; never globally prune
